results.title: Beyond efficiency: How artificial intelligence (AI) will reshape ...
results.content: # Beyond efficiency: How artificial intelligence (AI) will reshape scientific inquiry and the publication process. Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming how research is conceived, executed, published, and shared. This editorial examines the “elephant in the room”: the integration of AI across every stage of the research life cycle and publication pipeline. We trace AI’s expanding footprint on the author side, from sparking novel research ideas, mapping literature, and designing studies, to simulating data, analyzing results, and drafting manuscripts. We also consider AI’s growing role on the journal side, including automated manuscript triage, AI-assisted peer review, decision synthesis, and revision checks. And we discuss AI’s impact on research dissemination. Throughout, we highlight not only the unprecedented opportunities for creativity, efficiency, and accessibility, but also the ethical risks, such as epistemic homogenization, challenges to accountability, and the loss of scholarly craft. The question is no longer whether we want AI to shape the future of scholarship—it already is.

results.title: Content Studies: A New Academic Discipline for Analysing ...
results.content: For example, while computational linguistics focuses on text-based sentiment analysis, Content Studies could extend this approach to include multimodal datasets, analysing how visual and auditory elements interact with cultural narratives. As Content Studies emerges as a discipline, it must develop a coherent ethical framework addressing both research ethics and normative guidelines for content creation and distribution. This new “applied ethics” framework must go beyond traditional research ethics to address the unique challenges of studying, designing, and optimising multimodal content in algorithmically mediated environments. By integrating these ethical dimensions, Content Studies can develop normative frameworks that guide both research practices and content design principles, ensuring the discipline contributes positively to addressing societal challenges while adhering to rigorous ethical standards. By bridging the disciplines we saw at the beginning of this article, Content Studies follows these examples by responding to the growing complexity of digital, multimodal, and algorithmically mediated content systems. Content Studies: A New Academic Discipline for Analysing, Evaluating, and Designing Content in a Digital and AI-Driven Age. https://doi.org/10.1007/s13347-025-00877-6.

results.content: A comprehensive bibliometric assessment of the research on AI in higher education, beyond the classic design of a bibliometric analysis. Based on these descriptions, this study offers a synthesis and critique of research on AI in higher education on the following issues: (a) the use of AI to address educational disparities and foster inclusivity, (b) the ethics of AI-powered large language learning models and translation tools, and (c) AI literacy. Using quantitative topic modeling and qualitative analysis methods, this study describes: (1) the research landscape of AI in higher education and (2) the common topics of AI in higher education research, including topics related to inclusive education. A synthesis and critique of research on AI in higher education on the following issues: (a) the use of AI to address educational disparities and foster inclusivity, (b) the ethics of AI-powered large language learning models and translation tools, and (c) AI literacy.
